log.msg: measured, not assumed: a Playwright probe of four stacking configs shows plain (unpositioned) content is ALWAYS painted BEHIND a position:absolute;z-index:0 .background, never above it, regardless of DOM order -- flex-item children behave the same as plain block children (Chromium does not give flex items automatic positioned-like paint priority). Only content that is itself position:relative (or transformed) paints above, by DOM-order tiebreak within the same paint step. So the brief phrasing (no-wrapper usually works, breaks only for a positioned/transformed child) has it backwards for the common case -- the .content wrapper is the required habit, not a nice-to-have. Separately: pointer-events:none on .background means a click ALWAYS reaches the content underneath even in the broken-paint case (verified with elementFromPoint + a real page.mouse.click) -- visibility and clickability are decided by two different mechanisms here.

decision.question: how does the host that holds a .background layer get position:relative + isolation:isolate
options: an explicit class (.has-background) the caller must remember to add
:has(> .background) -- automatic, zero markup, the one-line promise holds literally
decision.chosen: both -- :has() automatic for the normal case, .has-background as the explicit escape hatch for when the layer is not a literal direct child
decision.why: :has() is already load-bearing elsewhere on this site (core/Page catalog rail, ext/Doc), so no browser-support reason to avoid it; the explicit class costs nothing extra and covers the one case :has() cannot see

decision.question: is the .background-content wrapper a nice habit (the brief's own framing) or actually required for ordinary content to be visible on top
options: a nice habit -- no wrapper mostly works, per the brief's wording (breaks only for a positioned/transformed child)
required -- measure it instead of assuming
decision.chosen: required, measured with a Playwright probe of 4 real layouts (task.jsonl earlier log + doc/decisions.md #2)
decision.why: CSS paints non-positioned in-flow content BEFORE any position:0 z-index sibling regardless of DOM order -- plain content and even flex-item content both lose to .background every time in Chromium; only content that is itself positioned or transformed wins, which is the opposite of the brief's framing
decision.rule: css#1 (read the cascade, don't assume it)

assign.outcome:
**A swappable background layer, ui/background, shipped with ten no-image kinds and a wall that proves each one readable.** `background(kind, options)` drops one `.background` div (absolute, inset 0, z-index 0, overflow hidden, pointer-events none) behind whatever a box already holds — `ground` `gradient` `dots` `grid` `stripes` `texture` `scatter` `blobs` `wave` `spotlight`, none of them images. The host needs nothing: `:has(> .background)` gives it `position: relative; isolation: isolate` automatically, with `.has-background` as the explicit escape hatch.

The wrapper question the owner raised was measured, not guessed: a Playwright probe of four real layouts found CSS paints plain, unpositioned content BEHIND a `z-index: 0` `.background` every time, regardless of DOM order — the opposite of what 'no wrapper usually works' would suggest. So `.background-content { position: relative; z-index: 1 }` is the required habit, not a nice-to-have; the page proves both rows side by side, live, and proves separately that a click still lands correctly either way (`pointer-events: none` makes clickability and visibility two different questions).

Contrast is measured live on the page itself (canvas-composited real computed colours, correct in both themes automatically) — every kind clears 4.5:1 with real margin: 7.8:1 (dots, the closest) to 17.4:1 (blobs, spotlight). Nothing needed a headings-only label. The proof pass on a private :8137 server found and fixed two real bugs along the way (both in doc/decisions.md §6): `wave` rendered as a solid black bar because `View.html()`'s Sanitizer API silently strips a class off an SVG `<path>` — switched to `.html_unsafe()`; `blobs`' first sizing swallowed a small demo card whole — shrunk to read as three corner glows at both a card and a hero. Final pass: 0 console errors and 0 horizontal scroll at 400/1280/3440 in both themes, all 10 wall-card buttons individually proven clickable through their background via `elementFromPoint`, a real click-through toggle, and the spotlight's `follow: true` pointer-tracking confirmed live.

![the wrapper demo, live](wrapper-demo.png)

**Left open, and why:** the page routes correctly (`/framework/ui/background/`, declared in `ui/page.js`'s `children:`) and its own breadcrumb back to UI works, but nothing on `/framework/ui/` currently LINKS to it — that page's only child links are its curated four-band `browse()` wall (six/six/six/five, load-bearing per that file's own comment), and this task's fence was 'the children line only' on `ui/page.js`, not its BANDS constant or its prose. Fixing this is a one-line job for whoever can edit that file next (a sentence + link, or a fifth band once it has a second member) — spelled out exactly in doc/decisions.md's Open section.
